record.paper_title: Open problems of the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings
record.original_question: When a graph G has a Type-A order or a Type-B order, can such an order be found in polynomial time? A Type-A order requires each vertex to have an odd number of earlier neighbors or none, and a Type-B order additionally permits a vertex to have an even number of earlier neighbors if it has no later neighbors.

evidence.quote: Problem 7.2 If a Type-A or Type-B order exists, can it be found in polynomial time?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph. For a linear ordering $v_1, v_2, \dots, v_n$ of $V$, call the vertices appearing before $v_i$ in the order the "earlier neighbors" of $v_i$ (restricted to $N(v_i)$), and those appearing after $v_i$ the "later neighbors" of $v_i$.

Define two types of vertex orderings:
- A Type-A order is a linear ordering of $V$ such that every vertex $v_i$ has either zero earlier neighbors or an odd number of earlier neighbors.
- A Type-B order is a linear ordering of $V$ such that every vertex $v_i$ satisfies at least one of: (i) it has an odd number of earlier neighbors, (ii) it has no earlier neighbors, or (iii) it has an even number of earlier neighbors and no later neighbors.

Question: Is there a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a graph $G$, decides whether $G$ admits a Type-A order (respectively, a Type-B order) and, if so, produces such an order?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in the collection of open problems from the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings (2024). No subsequent work resolving the polynomial-time recognition/construction of Type-A or Type-B vertex orders was located in available search results.
